title: Julian Calendar
intro: The Julian civil calendar divides a solar year into twelve familiar months with a simple four-year leap cycle.
structure: Years divisible by four are leap years, including century years. February has 29 days in a leap year and 28 otherwise, giving years of 366 or 365 days.
model: The provider extends consistent Julian arithmetic proleptically. For arithmetic year Y, month M and day D, set a=floor((14-M)/12), y=Y+4800-a, m=M+12*a-3. Then JDN = D+floor((153*m+2)/5)+365*y+floor(y/4)-32083. Its mean year is 365.25 days, longer than the tropical year; Julian and Gregorian dates gradually diverge.
example: Julian 1 January 2026 corresponds to Gregorian 14 January 2026. Julian 1900 and 2100 are leap years, unlike their Gregorian counterparts.
history: Julius Caesar's reform took effect in 45 BCE, replacing earlier Roman civil reckoning. Communities subsequently adopted Gregorian dating at different times; some religious traditions retain Julian dates.
limits: The model does not reproduce irregular early administration of leap days or regional Julian-to-Gregorian changeovers.
